institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several. First of all the academic oppurtunities to get the possibility to study at the best University in Europe in the field of International Relations. Secondly because I wanted to improve my french. Third and finally I believe Paris to be a great city to live in with having a rich culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High tempo and interesting courses. However I believe that the deadlines could have been spread out a bit more (it was basically 7 deadlines in one week in the end) and I also believe that some courses were lacking a bit of theoretical foundations and were to shallow/practical.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not so easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any specific information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is pretty difficult but we were lucky finding a nice apartment through a rental agency. I recommend checking agencies, and also to do it way in advance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very nice. You get to experience more of the real Paris in this way. Although just start look for accomodations in time!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got no assistance at all.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was a nightmare. I literally prepared for almost a full-working and still did not get any of the courses I wanted. This can be improved in every way.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it is on time. And as an exchange student you get the last spots in every course making it very difficult to get the courses you want. Therefore I just recommend to do ctrl+f as fast as you possibly can and then pray.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got an email with instructions but that did not help at all.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As unsuccessfull as you can possibly can be. I got 0 courses out 5.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am satisfied with the practical level of the courses making it very policyoriented. Although I think it sometimes was too practical.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was different where some courses demanded a lot and some not. Although the most demanding thing was to have a lot of deadlines in a short period of time in all of the courses at the same time. Stressful!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was a bit different in terms that the teaching at Sciences Po included way more oral participation during the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Energy Security 
Energy Diplomacy 
Demography and Global Politics 
Public Diplomacy & Communication 
Intelligence in national security processes 
Beyond Putin - civil mobilisation in former USSR republics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend intelligence in national security processes and Public Diplomacy and communication. First one because the teacher is amazing and the content of the course was super interesting. The second one because the teacher was very engaging and the tempo of study (including hand ins) were perfect.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot but I could for some reasons not register.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Boat party.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See all the museeums, go boat tripping and travel to Provence and Bordeaux!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be extrovert in your classes. Best way to get to know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Hard to measure since I got together with people from all around the world. 
But with that being said, without speaking good french it is difficult to integrate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Study french before you begin your exchange. French people can be rude if you don't speak the language.
2. Prepare for a very intense examine period with a lot of presentations and small deadlines. 
3. Enjoy your time and stay. It goes very fast and all of a sudden it is over. Thus don't put too much pressure on yourself but try to enjoy Paris and meet new people!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I met a lot of interesting and smart people from all over the world as well as that I got the chance to stay in one of the most exciting cities in the world for one semester!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language, the tight deadlines and to plan my schedule so that I could fit in both studies, work, applications, learning the language and doing fun stuff!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It should be possible as a master student in political science to study french and validate that course in my diploma. I don't see the reason why this is not possible since learning the french langauge only enrich my career as a political scientists.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
